We are pleased to have contributed to the discussion some ten years ago but recognise that the subject area has moved on. We would not recommend people starting to relate to our ontology now, and we look forward to migrating to some more authoritative one in due course.

Also, eastings & northings are best not confused with latitudes & longitudes. I have put in the definitions from the OS ontology: they are metres from an origin, in a defined "flat & square" projection.

I'm glad you've ignored the grid square classes in our ontologies!

commit message:
Add Finger-Cox-Jephcoat asymmetry using pseudo-Voight peak

Add new peak function based on that described in  Finger, Cox and Jephcoat (1994)
 J. Appl. Cryst. vol 27, pp 892-900.  An improved form of the normalisation
derivative (D in the above paper) as described in Hester (2013), J. Appl. Cryst.
(submitted) is included together with the accurate derivatives for H
and S described in the latter paper.  This asymmetry is essential for
modelling peaks from powder neutron diffraction facilities, and will also
improve fits to synchrotron and lab powder data.

In order to create the convoluted peakshape, Gauss-Legendre quadrature points
and weights are also included in a separate include file to avoid cluttering
the main code.

Signed-off-by: Marcin Wojdyr <wojdyr@gmail.com>

commit message:
* On wxGTK fitting was very slow, due to slow wxSafeYield(), which was called
  on every iteration. Now windows are disabled at the beginning of fitting,
  and wxYield is called only when needed.
  set_compute_ui(bool) function was added, which sets the function that is
  to be called at the beginning and end of long computations.
* New refresh-period option was added. After this time (in seconds), during
  fitting, GUI events are wxYield()ed and a short update about fitting progress
  is printed.
* Some class members where renamed from m_member to member_.
* GUI: to prevent redrawing plots multiple times after some operations (such as
  adding a peak), Refresh() is delayed: it's not called directly from
  refresh(), but from the first OnIdle() that comes after refresh().
* cosmetic changes to calling refresh() workflow
* On standard verbosity level, Lev-Mar shows much less informations (no info
  for every iteration).
* GUI: get_bg_color() was moved up to base class BufferedPanel.
* extended `define' syntax: added substitutions after where, e.g.:
  define FullGBE(k, alpha) = k * alpha * eta * (eta / tanh(eta) - ln (2*sinh(eta))) where eta = 2*pi/alpha * sin(theta/2), theta=x*pi/180

Parsing info command was changed. Instead of using Spirit, we use handcrafted
code that mostly just compares the first word after "info".
This fixes compilation problem with older gcc (compilation takes
forever with some compiler options).
This changes required changing hundreds of lines of code and a many libfityk
classes also had minor changes.
There are minor syntax and run-time changes, e.g. info commands[n:m]
with wrong indices generates error now. The test samples/test_syntax.fit
was modified appropriately.

commit message:
model.rst: remove confusion of F as sum vs F as set/list

It's a kind of confusing to overload F to stand for both set f_i and sum of them, as implied by formula https://fityk.nieto.pl/model.html#model-formula
Since the syntax ` F = %f +%g`, and output of `info F`, already implies F is sum of functions,
I think it's better to choose F to mean just sum of f_i, similarly for Z, and thus omit in docs the references to F/Z as sets/lists. (even if internally F, Z stand for some lists). It's okay to leave F[i] to mean ith function in the summation.

commit message:
Add support for s3WriteGzip option to gzip PCAPs on S3. (#1185)

* The writer-s3 plugin can now read files from S3 correctly.

* Coalesce fetches from S3 if possible. Currently does this if
there is less than a 32kbyte gap between packets

* Now passes the eslint checks....

* Have to move to having multiple blocks as zlib can buffer a lot of data internally. index.js also needs to handle multiple blocks as well.

* Compressed writing to S3 seems to work!

* Make sure that we return the right number of bytes for the pcap header

* Allow the selection of the S3 Storage-class. Turns out that the old default
(REDUCED_REDUNDANCY) is worse in every way (even cost) than STANDARD. Now
defaults to STANDARD, but you could choose INTELLIGENT_TIERING.

author: SG <13872653+mmguero@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
beginning work on https://github.com/aol/moloch/issues/1162, baseline comparison for connections visualization

consisting of (all in viewer.js):

1. factored out some code from buildSessionQuery into a determineQueryTimes
    function for calculating startTime, stopTime, and interval values
    given a req, and modified buildSessionQuery to call that function
    instead, as well as a new bit of code in buildConnections

2. In buildConnections, if network graph baseline is enabled
    (enabled: req.query.baseline=1, disabled:req.query.baseline=0 or undefined)
    then two queries will be run (ie., run buildSessionQuery->searchPrimary->process twice):
    first for the original specified time frame and second for the same time frame
    immediately preceding it.
  Nodes have an .inresult attribute where:
    Dec Bin  Description
    0 = 00 = not in either result set (although you'll never see these, obviously)
    1 = 01 = seen during the "current" time frame but not in the "baseline" time frame (ie., "new")
    2 = 10 = seen during the "baseline" time frame but not in the "current" time frame (ie., "old")
    3 = 11 = seen during both the "current" time frame and the "baseline" time frame
  This is only performed where startTime/startTime are defined, and never for "all" time range (date=-1).

commit message:
Fix issue #946, "hunt packet search jobs should skip sessions for which no PCAP exists" (#947)

Changed the initial query structure for the hunt session query from:

query: { bool: { filter: [{}] } },

to:

query: { bool: { must: [{ exists: { field: 'fileId' } }], filter: [{}] } },

In order to ensure that no sessions missing the fileId field are included in the results.

Tested it on my local moloch installation with both sessions from PCAP files (those containing fileId's) as well as those without, and I no longer get the crash. The correct matches seem to show up.

commit message:
Added three new fields for right click substitution:

%EXPRESSION% - the current search expression
%FIELD% - the field being right clicked, e.g. ip.src
%DATE% - the CGI params for the date of the current search.  Either date=X or startTime=X&stopTime=Y

This allows for right click pivot actions, e.g:

PIVOTIP=url:/?%DATE%&expression=ip+%3D%3D+%TEXT%;name:Pivot ip;category:ip

FIELDPIVOTIP=url:/?%DATE%&expression=%FIELD%+%3D%3D+%TEXT%;name:Pivot %FIELD%;category:ip

automatically correct it to "http.uri == //somesite.com."
In addition to user friendliness, this allows us to create
a right click pivot from http.location to http.uri in order
to follow HTTP redirect chains.

commit message:
Adds two new algorithms for selecting pcap directories when pcapDir has multiple values.

Adds a new config file key "pcapDirAlgorithm."  Valid values:

- round-robin: uses each directory in sequence and then starts over at the beginning of the list
- max-free-percent: chooses the directory on the filesystem with the highest percentage of free disk space
- max-free-bytes: chooses the directory on the filesystem with the highest number of available bytes

The default is "round-robin."

commit message:
Fix issue #946, "hunt packet search jobs should skip sessions for which no PCAP exists"

Changed the initial query structure for the hunt session query from:

query: { bool: { filter: [{}] } },

to:

query: { bool: { must: [{ exists: { field: 'fileId' } }], filter: [{}] } },

In order to ensure that no sessions missing the fileId field are included in the results.

Parse the Modbus TCP classified packets and extract the following:
* Protocol ID (always 0)
* Unit ID
* List of transaction IDs
* Number of separate transactions
* Length of data bytes according to the MBAP Header length field

* Improve the parser and classification, add parsing func and exception codes

commit message:
Adds two new algorithms for selecting pcap directories when pcapDir has multiple values. (#529)

Adds a new config file key "pcapDirAlgorithm."  Valid values:

- round-robin: uses each directory in sequence and then starts over at the beginning of the list
- max-free-percent: chooses the directory on the filesystem with the highest percentage of free disk space
- max-free-bytes: chooses the directory on the filesystem with the highest number of available bytes

The default is "round-robin."

author: Scott Schenkein <schenksj@yahoo.com>
commit message:
Statistics improvements (#1262)

1) SNF statistics are estimates and will significantly under-report packet read counts under higher volume conditions.  Since we're reading the actual packets in this module, we can easily calculate the correct packet count by keeping counters of the numbers of packets we've read.
2) Packet drops are calculated at the NIC level, not the application or ring.  This fix will reduce the over-reporting of drops (as reported by the SNF driver) by spreading the drops across all rings.  This does not, however, address incorrect reporting of drops if there are multiple SNF applications (Suricata and Moloch, for example) reporting on the same NIC (as in the case where Moloch is not allowing ring overruns and Suricata is, Moloch stats will include Suricata's drops).
3) A bug that was introduced in #1121 where statistics are always reported for the lower group of rings when capturing in multi-process mode.

commit message:
Implement --nooptimize argument for expire

Optimizing a sessions index can be very resource-intensive, and may take
a long time to complete unlike the rest of db.pl expire.  Watch for
Elasticsearch messages "now throttling indexes" to see if sessions
need to be optimized, or tune indicies.store.throttle.max_bytes_per_sec
(https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/guide/current/indexing-performance.html#segments-and-merging)

author: Daniel Roethlisberger <daniel@roe.ch>
commit message:
Fix SSL 2 version and remove fictional SSL 1 version (#3100)

* TLS/JA4: Fix SSL 2 version constant to 0x0002

SSL 2 uses a version field of 0x0002, not 0x0200.  This is confirmed not
only in the original Netscape spec [1] and RFC draft of the time [2],
but also in major implementations such as OpenSSL [3] and Wireshark [4].

An earlier version of the JA4 spec [5] also mistakenly used 0x0200 for
SSL 2 and 0x0100 for SSL 1.  This was fixed in [6] in August 2024.

[1] https://www-archive.mozilla.org/projects/security/pki/nss/ssl/draft02.html
[2] https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-hickman-netscape-ssl-00
[3] https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/OpenSSL_0_9_6m/ssl/ssl2.h#L66-L71
[4] https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/release-4.4/epan/dissectors/packet-tls-utils.h#L266-L277
[5] https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4/blob/main/technical_details/JA4.md#tls-and-dtls-version
[6] FoxIO-LLC/ja4#150

* TLS/JA4: Remove fictional SSL 1

SSL 1 was never actually deployed, the design was iterated upon to
become SSL 2 before it was released by Netscape [1] [2] [3] [4].  I
don't think it's public knowledge what the version field for SSL 1 would
have looked like, or if it even was two bytes large or at the same
offset on the wire; given that SSL 2 used 0x0002 it seems more likely to
have been 0x0001 than 0x0100.

Version field 0x0100, that is currently misattributed to SSL 1, was used
by an early pre-RFC4347 implementation of DTLS in OpenSSL before 0.9.8f
[5], when OpenSSL switched to the version field specified by RFC4347.
This use of 0x0100 is also reflected in Wireshark's TLS dissector [4]
(`DTLSV1DOT0_OPENSSL_VERSION`).

For these reasons, it seems to make sense to remove the fictional SSL 1
code entirely.

An earlier version of the JA4 spec [6] also mistakenly used 0x0200 for
SSL 2 and 0x0100 for SSL 1.  This was fixed in [7] in August 2024.

[1] https://www-archive.mozilla.org/projects/security/pki/nss/ssl/draft02.html
[2] https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-hickman-netscape-ssl-00
[3] https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/OpenSSL_0_9_6m/ssl/ssl2.h#L66-L71
[4] https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/release-4.4/epan/dissectors/packet-tls-utils.h#L266-L277
[5] https://github.com/openssl/openssl/compare/OpenSSL_0_9_8e...OpenSSL_0_9_8f
[6] https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4/blob/main/technical_details/JA4.md#tls-and-dtls-version
[7] FoxIO-LLC/ja4#150

* Fix test where pre 0.9.8f OpenSSL DTLS was misidentified as SSL 1

author: Andy Wick <awick@purple.org>
commit message:
Molochmagic (#552)

New magicMode and faster molochmagic

libmagic (libfile) can be slow on high http/smtp networks.  The new setting magicMode allows
* libmagic - default, same as before
* libmagicnotext - libmagic, but turns off text checks
* molochmagic - new molochmagic implementation
* none - no libmagic or molochmagic calls

molochmagic has about half the rules as libmagic.  It doesn't support regex rules or some of the more complex libmagic rules, however it is autogenerated from the libmagic files.  Most of the speed increase is from lookup tables.

author: Daniel Roethlisberger <daniel@roe.ch>
commit message:
TLS/JA4: Remove fictional SSL 1

SSL 1 was never actually deployed, the design was iterated upon to
become SSL 2 before it was released by Netscape [1] [2] [3] [4].  I
don't think it's public knowledge what the version field for SSL 1 would
have looked like, or if it even was two bytes large or at the same
offset on the wire; given that SSL 2 used 0x0002 it seems more likely to
have been 0x0001 than 0x0100.

Version field 0x0100, that is currently misattributed to SSL 1, was used
by an early pre-RFC4347 implementation of DTLS in OpenSSL before 0.9.8f
[5], when OpenSSL switched to the version field specified by RFC4347.
This use of 0x0100 is also reflected in Wireshark's TLS dissector [4]
(`DTLSV1DOT0_OPENSSL_VERSION`).

For these reasons, it seems to make sense to remove the fictional SSL 1
code entirely.

An earlier version of the JA4 spec [6] also mistakenly used 0x0200 for
SSL 2 and 0x0100 for SSL 1.  This was fixed in [7] in August 2024.

[1] https://www-archive.mozilla.org/projects/security/pki/nss/ssl/draft02.html
[2] https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-hickman-netscape-ssl-00
[3] https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/OpenSSL_0_9_6m/ssl/ssl2.h#L66-L71
[4] https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/release-4.4/epan/dissectors/packet-tls-utils.h#L266-L277
[5] https://github.com/openssl/openssl/compare/OpenSSL_0_9_8e...OpenSSL_0_9_8f
[6] https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4/blob/main/technical_details/JA4.md#tls-and-dtls-version
[7] FoxIO-LLC/ja4#150

author: Daniel Roethlisberger <daniel@roe.ch>
commit message:
TLS/JA4: Fix SSL 2 version constant to 0x0002

SSL 2 uses a version field of 0x0002, not 0x0200.  This is confirmed not
only in the original Netscape spec [1] and RFC draft of the time [2],
but also in major implementations such as OpenSSL [3] and Wireshark [4].

An earlier version of the JA4 spec [5] also mistakenly used 0x0200 for

author: Joe Moore <jpvlsmv@gmail.com>
commit message:
db.pl expire --nooptimize (#701)

* Define --nooptimize argument

* Implement --nooptimize argument for expire

Optimizing a sessions index can be very resource-intensive, and may take
a long time to complete unlike the rest of db.pl expire.  Watch for
Elasticsearch messages "now throttling indexes" to see if sessions
need to be optimized, or tune indicies.store.throttle.max_bytes_per_sec
(https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/guide/current/indexing-performance.html#segments-and-merging)

* --nooptimize skips the other/admin indexes

Even the small other indexes may take a long time to optimize due to locking,
one should periodically call db.pl optimize explicitly.

Grep more explicitly

With this change we will only grep for lines that *begin* with

This means we won't match lines with the setting `interfaceOps`, or
lines that contain `interface` and `=` in a comment.

commit message:
Tpacket3 multi-instance per-host support

Adding ability to use PACKET_FANOUT capabilities with AF_PACKET/tpacket3.  This uses PACKET_FANOUT_HASH to distribute packets between processes if more than one is listening on a given interface.  The config variable to enable this is `tpacketv3ClusterId` whose integer value must be globally unique on the interface.  The naming convention here mimics the implementation of analogous functionality in the moloch PF_RING support.

wrong call

author: Andy Wick <awick@purple.org>
commit message:
Reader schemes (#2571)

Introduce the concept of reader schemes to process pcap files from multiple local and report locations. Support for new schemes can be built into capture/viewer or added with a plugin. The schemes run in a single thread, which will make file processing faster then previous version. Switching to "scheme" mode vs libpcap-file mode is done either by using -r with any scheme OR the --scheme option. It is all or nothing, once in scheme mode non scheme supported items will not be used.

Currently we support:
file
s3 - normal s3 url
s3http(s) - s3http://host/bucket/key using the s3 protocol, supports minio or s3 obj urls
http(s) - http://host/path

author: Matt Carothers <matt.carothers@cox.com>
commit message:
Added three new fields for right click substitution:

%EXPRESSION% - the current search expression
%FIELD% - the field being right clicked, e.g. ip.src
%DATE% - the CGI params for the date of the current search.  Either date=X or startTime=X&stopTime=Y

This allows for right click pivot actions (search for the field in a new tab), e.g:

PIVOTIP=url:/?%DATE%&expression=ip+%3D%3D+%TEXT%;name:Pivot ip;category:ip

FIELDPIVOTIP=url:/?%DATE%&expression=%FIELD%+%3D%3D+%TEXT%;name:Pivot %FIELD%;category:ip

And right click drill actions (add the new field to the existing search in a new tab), e.g.:

FIELDDRILLIP=url:/?%DATE%&expression=%EXPRESSION%+%26%26+%FIELD%+%3D%3D+%TEXT%;name:Drill %FIELD%;category:ip

author: Scott Schenkein <schenksj@yahoo.com>
commit message:
Statistics improvements

1) SNF statistics are estimates and will significantly under-report packet read counts under higher volume conditions.  Since we're reading the actual packets in this module, we can easily calculate the correct packet count by keeping counters of the numbers of packets we've read.
2) Packet drops are calculated at the NIC level, not the application or ring.  This fix will reduce the over-reporting of drops (as reported by the SNF driver) by spreading the drops across all rings.  This does not, however, address incorrect reporting of drops if there are multiple SNF applications (Suricata and Moloch, for example) reporting on the same NIC (as in the case where Moloch is not allowing ring overruns and Suricata is, Moloch stats will include Suricata's drops).
3) A bug that was introduced in #1121 where statistics are always reported for the lower group of rings when capturing in multi-process mode.
